# Git Panel Scope

## How To Build

A GitPanelScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A GitPanelScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Title

null

## Counted

false

## Height

fit

## Scrolls

true

## Scrollbar

always

## Panel

It has no header: its contents start at its top edge, on the theme's base surface.
It shows no count of what it lists.
It is only as tall as its contents need, taking no more of its sidebar's height.
Its contents scroll on their own when they are taller than it, with a permanent scrollbar along its right, as the ScrollbarScope says.

## Concept

### Pitch

A very basic git panel for the repository the ProjectDirectoryScope is in, as the [GitScope](../../../scope/git/index.md#git-scope) knows it: see what has changed at a glance, write a commit message, commit, push, and pull.

### Shape

#### Description

A compact panel. It is shown only while the project is inside a git repository.

#### Look

The panel's top row, the branch, is its header: 32 pixels tall, on the ribbon's tab row colour, #333333 in dark mode. Beneath it, the panel's body is on the ribbon's command area colour, #222222 in dark mode, with 8 pixels of padding at either side and at the bottom, and 4 pixels between one thing and the next. There is no line between the header and the body, nor between the file tree and the header: the change of colour is the edge. Every box and button in it is square, with no rounded corners and no border, and the Pull and Push buttons are square too.

#### Sizing

The panel is only as tall as its header and body need, along the bottom of its sidebar, up to half the sidebar's height; the file tree takes the rest. It is never taller than its contents need, however it is sized: as its contents grow, such as when a commit note is added, it grows with them up to its most, its body scrolling beyond that, and as they shrink, such as when the notes are cleared by a commit, it shrinks straight back down to fit them.
The edge between the file tree and the panel's header can be dragged to resize it: dragged up, the panel may grow up to where the edge was dragged, but no taller than its contents need, and dragged down, it shrinks, as far as its header alone. The file tree always keeps at least 80 pixels. Once dragged, the panel's most is the height it was dragged to rather than half the sidebar, and it stays that height as the window is resized, giving way to the file tree's least height when the window is too short. The edge shows no line at rest, since the change of colour is the edge: while the pointer is over it, or it is being dragged, a line in the accent shows along it, and the cursor is a row-resize cursor.

#### Scrolling

When the panel is shorter than its contents, its header, the branch with Pull and Push, stays where it is, and its body, the summary, commit notes, message, Generate, and Commit, scrolls beneath it, with a [ScrollbarScope](../scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope) along its right. The body's colour runs all the way down the panel.

#### Branch

The top row shows a branch icon, then the branch from the [GitScope](../../../scope/git/index.md#git-scope), or "Detached HEAD", in regular text, beside how many commits it is ahead of its upstream (↑) and behind it (↓), muted, each only when not zero. At the right end are a Pull button, a cloud-download icon, and a Push button, a cloud-upload icon, ghost icon buttons with tooltips.

#### Summary

Below the branch, a line counts the [GitScope](../../../scope/git/index.md#git-scope)'s changes, leaving out any kind with none, as "2 modified · 1 untracked", or "No changes". At the right end of that line, how many lines were added (+, in green) and removed (−, in red). The count is in small, muted text. The files themselves are not listed, since the [FileTreeScope](../file-tree/index.md#file-tree-scope) shows them. The summary refreshes as the [GitScope](../../../scope/git/index.md#git-scope) does, and straight after anything the panel does.

#### Commit Notes

Above the message box, a box for each commit note, in the order they were added, on the ribbon's tab row colour, holding the note in small text that wraps onto as many lines as it needs, growing to fit it, and can be edited; <Enter> in a note starts a new line within it. A small button to remove it shows at its top right while it is hovered. Each task that adds a note, as the [PromptModesScope](../../../scope/prompt-mode/modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) says, adds a one-line summary of what it changed, once the harness has written it, quickly, in the same way as a written

##### Message

from what the task asked and the harness's own summary of what

it did, at most 72 characters in the imperative mood, as commit-note.pi, of the [BakedSystemPromptsScope](../../../scope/harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts-scope), asks. Notes are saved with the project's data, as the [ProjectDataScope](../../../scope/project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, as they are added, edited, and removed, so they survive a restart, and are never themselves committed.

#### Message

A commit message box, a [GrowingTextInputScope](../growing-text-input/index.md#growing-text-input-scope) growing to 10 rows at most, so it starts at a single row. On the tree's darkest surface, #111111 in dark mode, in the editor's monospace font, it reads "Commit Message…" while empty.

#### Writing AMessage

A "Generate" button, with a sparkles icon, on the ribbon's tab row colour, at the left of the row beneath the message box, has the harness write the commit message from what has changed, and puts it in the message box, replacing what was there. It is quick: a small, fast model, at low effort, with no tools, handed only the list of changed files and as much of the diff as fits in a small, fixed amount. The message is a summary line of at most 72 characters in the imperative mood, followed, only if it helps, by a few short bullet points, as commit-message.pi, of the [BakedSystemPromptsScope](../../../scope/harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts-scope), asks. The button is disabled while there are no changes.

#### Committing

A primary "Commit" button, at the right end of that row, on the ribbon's button colour, #444444 in dark mode, with no icon, commits every change, new files included. The commit message is what was typed, then a blank line, then each note that isn't blank as a line of its own starting "- "; with nothing typed, it is the notes alone. Once committed, the message box and the notes are cleared. It is disabled while there is neither a message nor a note, or there are no changes.

#### Pushing And Pulling

Push pushes the branch, setting its upstream on origin first if it has none.
Pull fetches the branch's upstream. With nothing new it says the branch is already up to date. When only the upstream has moved on, the branch fast-forwards to it. When both have moved on, the upstream is merged in automatically, as long as the merge has no conflicts. If it would conflict, the pull is cancelled before anything changes: the branch, its files, and the index stay exactly as they were, no merge is left in progress, and an error names the files that would have conflicted. Pull is disabled while the branch has no upstream.

#### Feedback

While the panel is committing, pushing, pulling, or writing a message, that button shows a spinner and the others are disabled. Committing, pushing, and pulling say so in a notification when they succeed; a pull says whether it was already up to date, pulled, or pulled and merged. Anything that fails says why in an error notification.

# Sidebar Scope

## How To Build

A SidebarScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A SidebarScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Concept

### Pitch

A column along the left or right of the main window, holding panels one above the other, each a tool for the work beside it.

### Shape

#### Description

Every sidebar is a sidebar, as its own scope says: it names the side it runs along, how wide it starts and how narrow it can be dragged, and the panels it holds, and those decide how it is drawn. It runs along its side, with a thin line down the edge where it meets what it sits beside, and is resized by dragging that edge. It holds its panels one above the other, across its full width, with a single thin line between one panel and the next.

#### Sidebars

- left: the [ProjectSidebarScope](../project-sidebar/index.md#project-sidebar-scope), to the left of the body, for finding your way around the project
- right: the [RightSidebarScope](../right-sidebar/index.md#right-sidebar-scope), at the right of the message list while a task runs

#### Panels

A panel is one tool in a sidebar, as its own scope says. What it is like follows from four things it names:

- its title: a panel with a title has a header reading it; one without has no header
- whether it is counted: a counted panel's header shows how many rows it lists, muted, at its right
- its height: a panel fills the height its sidebar's other panels leave, fits its contents, or shares the height left with the other panels that share it, by a line dragged between them
- whether it scrolls: one that scrolls has a [ScrollbarScope](../scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope) of its own when its contents are taller than it

#### Headers

A panel's header is slightly contrasting to the panel's body: the header is on the theme's raised surface, a small step toward the viewer, and the body on its base surface, as the sidebar is, so the header reads as part of the panel, marked off from its body, with no line between them.

## Sidebar

It runs along the right of what it sits beside, with a thin line down its left edge, where the two meet. It is resized by dragging that edge: it starts 260 pixels wide and can't be dragged narrower than 160.
It holds its panels one above the other, in the order it lists them, each across its full width. A single thin line, in the theme's line colour, lies between one panel and the next, never two, unless the next panel says its own change of colour is the edge. A panel that isn't shown for the moment takes no room and leaves no line.
It is on the theme's base surface, as its panels' bodies are.

## Concept

### Pitch

A second [SidebarScope](../sidebar/index.md#sidebar-scope), at the right of the message list and the chat input beneath it, that lists the spec files the running task references, so it's clear what part of the spec the harness is working from, and the constraints it has taken from it for the task.

### Shape

#### Description

It runs the full height of the body, beside the body's tab bar, the message list or file beneath it, and the chat input beneath those, which stops at its left edge rather than running beneath it. It keeps the width it was dragged to while the application runs.
Its two panels, the referenced files above the understanding, sit one above the other: the referenced files only as tall as their rows need, up to half the sidebar's height, scrolling beyond that, and the understanding filling the rest.

#### Look

The sidebar's body is on the ribbon's command area colour, #222222 in dark mode. Each panel's header is 32 pixels tall, on the darkest surface, #111111 in dark mode, as the file tree is, its title in small semibold text, 8 pixels from the left, with no count beside it. There is no line anywhere in it, not between a header and its body, nor between one panel and the next: the change of colour is the edge. The only line is the one down its left edge, where it meets the message list and the chat input, which is the handle it is resized by. In light mode the same steps are taken, as the ribbon's are.
Neither panel has a permanent scrollbar, since its column would break the 8 pixel inset: a panel shows its scrollbar only while its contents are taller than it, and none otherwise. When it shows, it is the same scrollbar as every other, as the [ScrollbarScope](../scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope) says.
A panel whose contents fit doesn't scroll at all, not even by a pixel, at any display scale or window size: it counts as taller than its contents need only once they overflow it by a whole pixel or more, so what is left over from rounding to the display's pixels never counts, and while they fit, it stays scrolled to its top. So neither the wheel nor a drag moves rows that all fit, and no scrollbar shows for them.

#### Showing

It is only there while a task is running: from the moment a task is sent from the Code, Chain, or Spec tab until its run is over. Questions from the Ask tab never show it, even when one is sent from the queue.
When a task starts, it slides out from the right edge of the message list and the chat input, growing from nothing to its width, its contents sliding into view from behind that edge as it does. When the run is over, it slides back the same way. The slide is quick and settles without bouncing. The message list and the chat input take the rest of the width, laid out anew only once the slide settles.

#### Description

One row per spec file the running task references, each listed once: first those its prompt imports from, then the rest in the order they are first referenced. /// Draws the line of a resize edge in group `group`, as gpui-kit does, and
/// notes the edge's hit area, which reaches [`RESIZE_REACH`] either side of it.
pub fn resize_edges(group: &'static str) -> ResizeHandleRenderer {
    Rc::new(move |edge: &ResizeHandleContext, _, cx| {
        let theme = cx.theme();
        let color = if edge.is_active() {
            theme.ring
        } else {
            theme.border
        };
        let horizontal = edge.axis() == Axis::Horizontal;
        let report = canvas(
            |_, _, _| {},
            move |bounds: Bounds<Pixels>, _, _, cx| {
                let (dx, dy) = if horizontal {
                    (RESIZE_REACH, px(0.))
                } else {
                    (px(0.), RESIZE_REACH)
                };
                let hit = Bounds::from_corners(
                    point(bounds.left() - dx, bounds.top() - dy),
                    point(bounds.right() + dx, bounds.bottom() + dy),
                );
                let key = format!(
                    "{group}@{:.0},{:.0}",
                    f32::from(bounds.left()),
                    f32::from(bounds.top())

                register_resize(key.into(), hit, cx);
            },
        )
        .absolute()
        .size_full();
        Some(

                .relative()
                .flex_none()
                .bg(color)
                .when(horizontal, |line| line.h_full().w(px(1.)))
                .when(!horizontal, |line| line.w_full().h(px(1.)))
                .child(report)
                .into_any_element(),
        )
    })

impl MainWindow {
    /// The file tree, with the git panel beneath it while it shows, the tree
    /// taking what it leaves. The git panel shrinks to fit its contents,
    /// growing up to half the sidebar, or, once the edge between them is
    /// dragged, up to where it was dragged. The git panel's header's change of colour is that edge, so no
    /// line is drawn there, but one shows while it is hovered or dragged.
    fn render_project_sidebar(&self, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> AnyElement {
        if !self.git_panel.read(cx).is_shown() {
            return div()
                .size_full()
                .child(self.sidebar.clone())
                .into_any_element();
        }
        let ring = cx.theme().ring;
        use gpui_kit::base::ElementExt as _;
        let edge = div()
            .id("git-resize")
            .group("git-resize")
            .absolute()
            .top(-GIT_EDGE_REACH)
            .left_0()
            .right_0()
            .h(GIT_EDGE_REACH * 2.)
            .flex()
            .items_center()
            .cursor_row_resize()
            .on_prepaint(|bounds, _, cx| {
                crate::hit_areas::register_resize("git-resize".into(), bounds, cx)
            })
            .child(
                div()
                    .w_full()
                    .h(px(1.))
                    .group_hover("git-resize", |line| line.bg(ring)),
            )
            .on_drag(GitResize, |_, _, _, cx| cx.new(|_| gpui_kit::EmptyView));
        // Lets UI tests find the sidebar; inert in normal builds.
        gpui_kit::TestSupportExt::test_support(gpui_kit::component::v_flex().id("project-sidebar"))
            .size_full()
            .on_drag_move(
                cx.listener(|this, event: &DragMoveEvent<GitResize>, _, cx| {
                    let bounds = event.bounds;
                    // The tree keeps its least height, the git panel its header.
                    let most = (bounds.size.height - MIN_FILE_TREE_HEIGHT)
                        .max(crate::git_panel::MIN_HEIGHT);
                    let height = (bounds.bottom() - event.event.position.y)
                        .clamp(crate::git_panel::MIN_HEIGHT, most);
                    if this.git_height != Some(height) {
                        this.git_height = Some(height);
                        cx.notify();
                    }
                }),
            )
            .child(div().flex_1().min_h_0().child(self.sidebar.clone()))
            .children(crate::sidebar::between(
                true,
                crate::git_panel::COLOUR_IS_EDGE,
                cx,
            ))
            .child(
                gpui_kit::component::v_flex()
                    .relative()
                    .w_full()
                    // As tall as its contents, up to its most, giving way to
                    // the tree however the window is resized.
                    .flex_shrink(1.)
                    .min_h(crate::git_panel::MIN_HEIGHT)
                    .max_h(match self.git_height {

                    })

            )

    }
}

            }))
            .on_action(cx.listener(|this, _: &ViewDivergenceReports, window, cx| {

            }))
            .on_action(cx.listener(|this, _: &ribbon::ShowTab1, _, cx| this.show_ribbon_tab(0, cx)))
            .on_action(cx.listener(|this, _: &ribbon::ShowTab2, _, cx| this.show_ribbon_tab(1, cx)))
            .on_action(cx.listener(|this, _: &ribbon::ShowTab3, _, cx| this.show_ribbon_tab(2, cx)))
            .on_action(cx.listener(|this, _: &ribbon::ShowTab4, _, cx| this.show_ribbon_tab(3, cx)))
            .on_action(cx.listener(|this, _: &ribbon::ShowTab5, _, cx| this.show_ribbon_tab(4, cx)))
            .on_action(cx.listener(|this, _: &ribbon::ToggleRibbon, _, cx| {

            .children(Root::render_dialog_layer(window, cx))

    }

## Sidebar

It runs along the right of what it sits beside, with a thin line down its left edge, where the two meet. It is resized by dragging that edge: it starts 260 pixels wide and can't be dragged narrower than 160.
It holds its panels one above the other, in the order it lists them, each across its full width. A panel that isn't shown for the moment takes no room and leaves no line.
It is on the theme's base surface, as its panels' bodies are.

## Concept

### Pitch

A second [SidebarScope](../sidebar/index.md#sidebar-scope), at the right of the message list and the chat input beneath it, that lists the spec files the running task references, so it's clear what part of the spec the harness is working from, and the constraints it has taken from it for the task.

### Shape

#### Description

It runs the full height of the body, beside the body's tab bar, the message list or file beneath it, and the chat input beneath those, which stops at its left edge rather than running beneath it. It keeps the width it was dragged to while the application runs.
Its two panels, the referenced files above the understanding, sit one above the other: the referenced files only as tall as their rows need, up to half the sidebar's height, scrolling beyond that, and the understanding filling the rest.

#### Look

The sidebar's body is on the ribbon's command area colour, #222222 in dark mode. Each panel's header is 32 pixels tall, on the darkest surface, #111111 in dark mode, as the file tree is, its title in small semibold text, 8 pixels from the left, with no count beside it. There is no line anywhere in it, not between a header and its body, nor between one panel and the next: the change of colour is the edge. The only line is the one down its left edge, where it meets the message list and the chat input, which is the handle it is resized by. In light mode the same steps are taken, as the ribbon's are.
Neither panel has a permanent scrollbar, since its column would break the 8 pixel inset: a panel shows its scrollbar only while its contents are taller than it, and none otherwise. When it shows, it is the same scrollbar as every other, as the [ScrollbarScope](../scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope) says.
A panel whose contents fit doesn't scroll at all, not even by a pixel, at any display scale or window size: it counts as taller than its contents need only once they overflow it by a whole pixel or more, so what is left over from rounding to the display's pixels never counts, and while they fit, it stays scrolled to its top. So neither the wheel nor a drag moves rows that all fit, and no scrollbar shows for them.

#### Showing

It is only there while a task is running: from the moment a task is sent from the Code, Chain, or Spec tab until its run is over. Questions from the Ask tab never show it, even when one is sent from the queue.
When a task starts, it slides out from the right edge of the message list and the chat input, growing from nothing to its width, its contents sliding into view from behind that edge as it does. When the run is over, it slides back the same way. The slide is quick and settles without bouncing. The message list and the chat input take the rest of the width, laid out anew only once the slide settles.

/// Draws the line of a resize edge in group `group`, as gpui-kit does, and
/// notes the edge's hit area, which reaches [`RESIZE_REACH`] either side of it.
pub fn resize_edges(group: &'static str) -> ResizeHandleRenderer {
    Rc::new(move |edge: &ResizeHandleContext, _, cx| {
        let theme = cx.theme();
        let color = if edge.is_active() {
            theme.ring
        } else {
            theme.border
        };
        let horizontal = edge.axis() == Axis::Horizontal;
        let report = canvas(
            |_, _, _| {},
            move |bounds: Bounds<Pixels>, _, _, cx| {
                let (dx, dy) = if horizontal {
                    (RESIZE_REACH, px(0.))
                } else {
                    (px(0.), RESIZE_REACH)
                };
                let hit = Bounds::from_corners(
                    point(bounds.left() - dx, bounds.top() - dy),
                    point(bounds.right() + dx, bounds.bottom() + dy),
                );
                let key = format!(
                    "{group}@{:.0},{:.0}",
                    f32::from(bounds.left()),
                    f32::from(bounds.top())
                );
                register_resize(key.into(), hit, cx);
            },
        )
        .absolute()
        .size_full();
        Some(
            div()
                .relative()
                .flex_none()
                .bg(color)
                .when(horizontal, |line| line.h_full().w(px(1.)))
                .when(!horizontal, |line| line.w_full().h(px(1.)))
                .child(report)
                .into_any_element(),
        )
    })

    /// The file tree, with the git panel beneath it while it shows, the tree
    /// taking what it leaves. The git panel shrinks to fit its contents,
    /// growing up to half the sidebar, or, once the edge between them is
    /// dragged, up to where it was dragged. The git panel's header's change of colour is that edge, so no
    /// line is drawn there, but one shows while it is hovered or dragged.
    fn render_project_sidebar(&self, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> AnyElement {
        if !self.git_panel.read(cx).is_shown() {
            return div()
                .size_full()
                .child(self.sidebar.clone())
                .into_any_element();
        }
        let ring = cx.theme().ring;
        use gpui_kit::base::ElementExt as _;
        let edge = div()
            .id("git-resize")
            .group("git-resize")
            .absolute()
            .top(-GIT_EDGE_REACH)
            .left_0()
            .right_0()
            .h(GIT_EDGE_REACH * 2.)
            .flex()
            .items_center()
            .cursor_row_resize()
            .on_prepaint(|bounds, _, cx| {
                crate::hit_areas::register_resize("git-resize".into(), bounds, cx)
            })
            .child(
                div()
                    .w_full()
                    .h(px(1.))
                    .group_hover("git-resize", |line| line.bg(ring)),
            )
            .on_drag(GitResize, |_, _, _, cx| cx.new(|_| gpui_kit::EmptyView));
        // Lets UI tests find the sidebar; inert in normal builds.
        gpui_kit::TestSupportExt::test_support(gpui_kit::component::v_flex().id("project-sidebar"))
            .size_full()
            .on_drag_move(
                cx.listener(|this, event: &DragMoveEvent<GitResize>, _, cx| {
                    let bounds = event.bounds;
                    // The tree keeps its least height, the git panel its header.
                    let most = (bounds.size.height - MIN_FILE_TREE_HEIGHT)
                        .max(crate::git_panel::MIN_HEIGHT);
                    let height = (bounds.bottom() - event.event.position.y)
                        .clamp(crate::git_panel::MIN_HEIGHT, most);
                    if this.git_height != Some(height) {
                        this.git_height = Some(height);
                        cx.notify();
                    }
                }),
            )
            .child(div().flex_1().min_h_0().child(self.sidebar.clone()))
            .children(crate::sidebar::between(
                true,
                crate::git_panel::COLOUR_IS_EDGE,
                cx,
            ))
            .child(
                gpui_kit::component::v_flex()
                    .relative()
                    .w_full()
                    // As tall as its contents, up to its most, giving way to
                    // the tree however the window is resized.
                    .flex_shrink(1.)
                    .min_h(crate::git_panel::MIN_HEIGHT)

    fn render(&mut self, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> impl IntoElement {

            .relative()
            .size_full()

                if let Some(palette) = &this.palette
                    && palette.read(cx).is_open(window, cx)
                {
                    palette.update(cx, |palette, cx| palette.cancel(window, cx));
                    return;
                }
                this.open_divergence(Opening::Analyze, window, cx)
            }))
            .on_action(cx.listener(|this, _: &ViewDivergenceReports, window, cx| {
                this.open_divergence(Opening::ViewReports, window, cx)
            }))
            .on_action(cx.listener(|this, _: &ribbon::ShowTab1, _, cx| this.show_ribbon_tab(0, cx)))
            .on_action(cx.listener(|this, _: &ribbon::ShowTab2, _, cx| this.show_ribbon_tab(1, cx)))
            .on_action(cx.listener(|this, _: &ribbon::ShowTab3, _, cx| this.show_ribbon_tab(2, cx)))
            .on_action(cx.listener(|this, _: &ribbon::ShowTab4, _, cx| this.show_ribbon_tab(3, cx)))
            .on_action(cx.listener(|this, _: &ribbon::ShowTab5, _, cx| this.show_ribbon_tab(4, cx)))

content.text:
Both sidebar resize edges now light up in the accent colour while you hover over them, not just while you drag them, the same way the git panel's edge does.

**What changed:** the left sidebar's edge and the right sidebar's edge are both drawn by `resize_edges` in `src/hit_areas.rs`. It only switched to the accent colour during a drag. The drag handle it draws inside is already grouped as `"handle"` by the UI library (gpui-kit), so I added a hover style on that group to turn the line accent-coloured. The colour at rest is the same as before, and the cursor was already a column-resize cursor.

**Checked:** it builds, and the `hit_areas` and `scrollbar` tests pass. I haven't run the app to see the hover myself.

**Spec gap:** the git panel spec describes its accent line on hover, but the sidebar, project sidebar and right sidebar specs only mention a thin line you drag. Since I'm not to edit the spec, the code now does something the spec doesn't describe. If you want the two kept in step, the line to add is in the Sidebar spec's Description: "while the pointer is over the edge, or it is being dragged, its line shows in the accent."

The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1790706536-Prompt_f2d3d6d9e3f54d89.understanding.md`.
